work.name: Bitshala
work.description: Bitshala is a grassroots initiative led by Indian Bitcoiners that trains and supports developers of open-source Bitcoin software. I am a Bitshala Fellow, continuing my work on [SeedSigner](https://github.com/SeedSigner/seedsigner), an air-gapped Bitcoin signing device, after two Summer of Bitcoin terms on it.

highlights.text: Review and test pull requests across the SeedSigner repos: the app, the OS and the translations.
Review and test the new microcontroller port (ESP32-P4, MicroPython, LVGL) on real hardware.
Contribute features and fixes to the app and the OS, most recently in PSBT handling and localization.
Help with triage and release chores.

Published [seedsigner-devkit](https://github.com/Chaitanya-Keyal/seedsigner-devkit), tools for developing on real hardware: one-command deploy to a Pi dev device, HDMI mirror, USB keyboard as buttons, and log, REPL and flashing for ESP32-P4 boards.

x.oneLiner: fellowship to keep working on SeedSigner

work.name: OnFinance AI
work.description: OnFinance builds an AI compliance platform for financial institutions. I mainly worked on the agent side of it: pipelines that read regulation so compliance teams do not have to, and the plumbing that keeps autonomous agents reliable enough for production use.

highlights.text: Started the platform's AI agent service and wrote most of it: LangGraph agents that automate circular analysis for regulators like SEBI and RBI, cutting interpretation time by ~90%.
Designed a search agent over 2000+ circulars and 500,000+ clauses that answers with citations instead of raw matches.
Started the rebuild of that service as a new agent runtime with resumable, checkpointed, parallel runs, and was its main contributor through launch.
Replaced bounding-box PDF parsing with structured clause extraction driven by a sandboxed coding agent.
The new runtime replaced the old service in production and now hosts 90+ agent nodes.
Fixed agent failures found in production traces: a guard against tool-call loops, batching for slow cascades, and recovery for runs orphaned by pod restarts.
Also built a change-management agent for amended circulars, a project-planning agent, per-organization feature gates, and most of the nightly workflow that patches service images against CVEs.

work.name: Summer of Bitcoin
work.description: Summer of Bitcoin places students into open-source Bitcoin projects through a competitive selection: about 50 to 60 are chosen globally each year from roughly 5,000 applicants. **Selected twice**, both times to work on [SeedSigner](https://github.com/SeedSigner/seedsigner), an air-gapped Bitcoin signing device.

highlights.text: Now one of the top contributors to SeedSigner, involved in 110+ PRs and issues.
Automated SeedSigner’s localization (i18n) workflows to remove routine burden from translators, contributors, and maintainers while improving review quality and safety.
Built CI tooling to detect missing and stale translations across supported languages, catching errors pre-review and cutting manual maintainer effort.
Extended BIP-85 support on SeedSigner to enable direct child seed loading.
Refactored the Python codebase for maintainability and shipped UI alerts warning users of high transaction fees.
Reviewed pull requests and resolved edge-case bugs across different parts of the project.

Cut API latency from ~5s to ~1s through architectural changes and resource management.
Built an agentic booking system integrating ONDC, Uber, and Rapido through browser automation.
Maintain the [instrument booking portal](https://github.com/CAL-BPHC/onlineCAL) used by 1,100+ researchers; built usage panels, reports and CI/CD.

projects.name: SeedSigner
projects.description: SeedSigner is a DIY, air-gapped, stateless Bitcoin signing device built with off-the-shelf parts. I have contributed across two Summer of Bitcoin terms, and stayed on after both, working on features, bugfixes, release chores, PR review and translations.

highlights.text: Automated the localization workflow across the code and translation repos, so a change to the source strings no longer means routine work for translators, contributors and maintainers.
Built that automation to be safe on untrusted fork PRs: read-only jobs run the contributed code without secrets, and a separate trusted job validates their output before anything is written.
Built CI tooling that detects missing and stale translations across the 20+ supported languages, catching errors before review rather than after it.
Added a per-PR screenshot review page, so a translation can be judged in the screen it actually lands in.
Extended BIP-85 support to enable direct child seed loading on-device.
Refactored the Python codebase for maintainability and shipped UI alerts warning users of abnormally high transaction fees.
Added the Hindi translation, made hard-coded strings translatable, and did the 0.8.7 version bump.

projects.name: satbook
projects.description: A single-user Bitcoin portfolio tracker that doubles as an India VDA tax engine. Every income, buy, sell, spend and self-transfer goes into one ledger, and holdings, break-even, unrealized P/L and Schedule VDA figures are recomputed from it on every read.

highlights.text: Computes tax the conservative way under s.115BBH: flat 30% plus cess, cost of acquisition only, losses ring-fenced, network fees neither taxed nor deducted.
Derives the third value from any two of amount, rate and fiat value, and autofills the timestamp, amounts and fee from a pasted on-chain txid.
Fetches the historical rate for backdated entries itself, converting through USD or EUR when that is the only quote available.

x.oneLiner: self-hosted Bitcoin passbook and India VDA tax engine

projects.name: Resume Builder
projects.description: A local-first resume builder that keeps one library of everything you have done and composes any number of resumes from it.

highlights.text: Runs pdfTeX as WebAssembly in a Web Worker with a 13 MB trimmed TeX tree, giving sub-second previews with no server.
No data leaves the user's device: Uses IndexedDB, no accounts, no tokens; publishing to a site hands the file to GitHub's own editor.
Shipped editing features like fit-to-one-page that probes denser layouts, reviewer hints for weak or number-free bullets, undo, and drag-and-drop ordering.

projects.name: BioHue
projects.description: The readout app for a colorimetric wound-dressing study, built for the research group running it. Photograph a dressing, and the app extracts the sample region, measures its colour and classifies it against the thresholds calibrated for that substrate, so the reading does not depend on who is looking at it.

highlights.text: Isolates the region of interest by thresholding saturation in HSV, refining the mask with morphological opening and closing, then taking the largest contour.
Detects glare by brightness and repaints it from the average of the surrounding unaffected pixels, so a reflection cannot skew the reading.
Crops that region to a circle, so every sample is measured over the same shape however the photo was framed.
Applies a per-substrate formula to the separated RGB channels and classifies the result against calibrated thresholds.

x.oneLiner: colorimetric readout app for a wound-dressing study

projects.name: Chrono2GCal
projects.description: Takes a Chronofactorem timetable ID and writes the whole semester into Google Calendar: classes with their rooms and instructors, exams with the seat allotted to that student, and nothing at all on holidays.
projects.entity: Personal project, used by BITS students

highlights.text: Pulls the timetable from Chronofactorem directly, so a student supplies only the four-character ID.
Parses the seating-arrangement PDFs the timetable division publishes to find each student allotted exam room.
Clears classes on holidays and exam days, rather than leaving a calendar that quietly disagrees with the semester.
Reads colours, reminders, titles and descriptions from a JSON file, and bulk-deletes by filter when a semester changes.

x.oneLiner: syncs BITS timetables into Google Calendar

projects.name: Arcade
projects.description: Two board games played online against other people. Room and game events travel over a TCP protocol built for it, a Flask API handles accounts, and the client is Tkinter.

highlights.text: Designed the wire protocol carrying room and game events between the server and every connected player.
Implemented full Monopoly and Chess rules, and the shared state each client has to be kept in step with.
Built accounts, profile pictures and lifetime statistics behind a Flask API backed by MySQL.
Implemented a custom dark theme for Tkinter, and designed the entire UI with custom widgets.
